import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 31

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/31](https://www.erdosproblems.com/31)
- [Er56] Erdős, P., *Problems and results in additive number theory*. Colloque sur la Théorie des
  Nombres, Bruxelles, 1955 (1956), 127-137.
- [Er59] Erdős, P., *Über einige Probleme der additiven Zahlentheorie*. Sammelband zu Ehren des 250.
  Geburtstages Leonhard Eulers (1959), 116-119.
- [Er65b] Erdős, Paul, *Some recent advances and current problems in number theory*. Lectures on
  Modern Mathematics, Vol. III (1965), 196-244.
- [Er73] Erdős, P., *Problems and results on combinatorial number theory*. A survey of combinatorial
  theory (Proc. Internat. Sympos., Colorado State Univ., Fort Collins, Colo., 1971) (1973), 117-138.
- [Lo54] Lorentz, G. G., *On a problem of additive number theory*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (1954), 838-841.
-/

namespace Erdos31

open Filter
open scoped Pointwise

/--
Given any infinite set $A\subset \mathbb{N}$ there is a set $B$ of density $0$ such that $A+B$ contains all except finitely many integers.

Conjectured by Erdős and Straus. Proved by Lorentz [Lo54].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos31.lean"]
theorem erdos_31 : ∀ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite →
    ∃ B : Set ℕ, B.HasDensity 0 ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ A + B := by
  sorry

end Erdos31

reformulations.difference: The coverage condition uses eventual membership in `atTop` on ℕ rather than explicitly stating a finite exceptional set or a sufficiently-large threshold.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: On ℕ, `Nat.cofinite_eq_atTop` gives `(∀ᶠ n in atTop, n ∈ A + B) ↔ (A + B)ᶜ.Finite`. Also, `Filter.eventually_atTop` and `Set.mem_add` give the equivalent formulation `∃ N, ∀ n ≥ N, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, a + b = n`. These equivalences were proved in the scratch file and match the sufficiently-large formulation in [Er56, §4] and [Er59, §3].

sources_consulted: [Er56] Erdős, Problems and results in additive number theory (1956), §4, pp. 132–134: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1956-17.pdf
[Er59] Erdős, Über einige Probleme der additiven Zahlentheorie (1959), §3, pp. 117–118: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1959-27.pdf
[Er65b] Erdős, Some recent advances and current problems in number theory (1965), passage on the Erdős–Straus conjecture and Lorentz's theorem: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1965-17.pdf
[Er73] Erdős, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory (1973), §12, pp. 133–134: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1973-21.pdf
Erdős problem database description and status table: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/teorth/erdosproblems/main/README.md
OpenAlex bibliographic and access metadata for [Lo54]: https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9939-1954-0063389-3
review.notes:
The sole declaration faithfully states the conjecture reproduced in the cited Erdős papers. In particular, [Er59] explicitly requires B(x)/x → 0, confirming natural density. Checked real division, finiteness of the interval cardinalities, nonvacuity, and the empty/zero/small-cutoff cases in /workspace/review/scratch.lean. The solved status agrees with the primary literature and the database's 'proved (Lean)' record.

The linked proof targets Lean 4.29.1. A scratch compatibility port to the installed 4.33.1, changing proofs but no mathematical statements, compiled with only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. A separate compiled equivalence confirms that its density definition and theorem type match the repository statement.

Access limitation: the current erdosproblems.com page and Lorentz's publisher PDF returned Cloudflare challenges. Mathematical verification therefore used the four cited Erdős papers directly; Lorentz's paper itself was accessible only through bibliographic metadata.
